svg.title: Plain block versus residual block on a 4 by 4 feature map
svg.desc: Left: edge map x goes through layers only and the layers must rebuild the whole output H(x). Right: the layers compute only the correction F(x), and x + F(x) gives edges kept plus corner added.
svg.text: Plain block vs residual block on the same feature map
x has no direct route to the output
x arrives by the shortcut; the layers add only F(x)
Reading the figure and the terms
Teal = features already in x, amber = new content, gray = zero. Numbers are illustrative; a real F(x) has many values across many channels.
In the plain block the layers must produce the whole map themselves, including the edges that were already correct in x.
F(x) is only the output of the block’s layers (here just the +2 correction). The block’s output is x + F(x).
“Skip” does not mean skipping computation: the layers still run and F(x) is used. Only the copy of x goes around them.
“Residual” means the remainder: F(x) = H(x) − x. The layers learn the remainder because the shortcut already supplies x.
